A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAR research. The full main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original safeguard evaluations, red-teaming results, benign fine-tuning experiments, and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a refusal-training diagnostic in Appendix D.5 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the two-stage safeguarding procedure, training objectives, and implementation of TAR remain unchanged. DPO-based refusal training was already present in v1; its new diagnostic does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Coverage remains WMDP biosecurity, chemical security and cybersecurity, MMLU, HarmBench/MT-Bench refusal evaluation, and benign economics fine-tuning. The new DPO analysis uses the existing refusal task; the retain-data specification is revised within retained evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1, 2, 11, and 12 and the baseline descriptions are unchanged. However, v3 adds Rosati et al.'s Immunization work and says the 'latter two works' were covered by its comparisons, without an identifiable Immunization setup or result. Whether an additional comparator was actually evaluated is unresolved.

E3.justification: v3 adds average DPO win-rate tracking during refusal training. Appendix F.1 also explicitly specifies Pile-bio Retain data for test-time evaluation, whereas v1 Appendix E.1 referred to the mixed training Retain corpus defined in D.2. This revises the reported setup; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.5 and Figure 7 add an analysis of whether refusal preference persists along training-time attack trajectories. The existing benign fine-tuning, targeted patching, inner-loop-length, component-ablation, and loss-weight analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing averaging practices remain unchanged, and the new DPO trajectory supplies no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing tabular results are unchanged, including TAR's 63.9% average post-attack HarmBench ASR in Tables 2 and 11. New Figure 7 reports increasing refusal win-rates during training and final inner-loop trajectories that flatten near 1.0.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions, tamper-resistance definitions, Equations 1–3, and appendix loss formulations are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: TAR provides substantial tamper-resistance while preserving benign capabilities and demonstrates that progress on open-weight safeguards is tractable.

C2.justification: Appendix D.5 interprets the new refusal-training trajectories as evidence that TAR can satisfy complex resistance objectives and potentially accommodate other useful objectives. The existing limitations, capability tradeoffs, and discussion of unsuccessful defenses remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 makes the test-time Retain corpus explicit and distinguishes it from the mixed training corpus in Appendix F.1. Hardware, implementation optimizations, dataset-construction details, and code/model access information otherwise remain unchanged after appendix renumbering.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Immunization against Harmful Fine-tuning Attacks, Targeted Latent Adversarial Training, and Shadow Alignment. Section 2 also revises its characterization of Vaccine and qualifies the evaluation coverage and robustness of concurrent defenses.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Author Contributions appendix, moves targeted patching before the inner-loop-length analysis, and makes limited paragraph and terminology revisions. Most main-text and appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the DPO trajectory Figure 7; v1's chemical/cybersecurity heatmaps become Figure 8 with unchanged content. Figure 3's caption specifies the training duration, and appendix figures and tables are locally repositioned and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The new refusal-training diagnostic fills a narrow explanatory gap in v1, while the added prior-work coverage and more explicit evaluation documentation improve completeness. The gains are limited: benchmark evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged, and the asserted Immunization comparison remains insufficiently documented.
